items.subject: Updates to your branded content toolkit on YouTube
items.summary: YouTube added tools to help disclose branded content partnerships.
items.body:
Joined pairs of jigsaw puzzle pieces and floating coins.

<https://c.gle/AGSJxQyP2uJQptBNqQzFb9pWq2yuV0xib6IWTWdBWdE2xWA6CvRimLVsjRby9i1A04X_bpIsMR5zW8ivaruj2mrYeXoNRewRAY2ej0fLEc

Supporting your
  brand partnerships
on YouTube

We know brand partnerships are critical for growing your business and  
deepening your connection with your community. To help you maintain  
transparency with viewers and strengthen relationships with brand partners,  
we've introduced several features that streamline how you disclose paid  
content.

These updates include refreshed, viewer-facing labels for branded content,  
as well as age and location controls to help you navigate regional  
requirements. As we shared in September, we're also starting to roll out  
automated detection for undeclared brand deals and may start auto-labeling  
content we detect as paid promotion that wasn't declared.

While these tools are designed to help, as a creator, you are responsible  
for ensuring your branded content is properly disclosed and follows our  
policies and all legal regulatory requirements. We're committed to  
providing the tools and features you need to support your business every  
step of the way.

Learn more

<https://c.gle/AGSJxQyQxkE8vxFE8CVL6_JcUkep7snF-zq-iHMx9MfFD0bRsKE_ABaNiwJ0MOegcAFcw3CeJ3OqmxNQepA8pmZhBRYMQ6NirLVPHdhsD4

What's in your branded content toolkit?

Clarified global policy

In September we updated YouTube policy guidelines to standardize  
terminology around “branded content” and clarify regulatory disclosure  
obligations and applicable Google Ads policy, so you know what's expected  
for content that features brand partners.

Redesigned viewer labels

Viewers now see a refreshed, simpler paid promotion label. We've updated  
the design to remove the “$” sign for better global appeal, keeping your  
audience informed about paid promotions while maintaining trust and  
transparency.

Age and location controls

You can now set age and country-level location restrictions for your  
videos. This means you won't have to pass on a brand partnership because of  
strict demographic or regional constraints.

Automated detection

Manual disclosure of branded content is still required, and we're starting  
to roll out automated detection for paid promotions. If our systems detect  
that a video contains a paid promotion that wasn't declared, we may notify  
you and proactively apply a disclosure label. You may have the option to  
remove the disclosure in YouTube Studio.

Learn more

<https://c.gle/AGSJxQwkV8IZsy6RNifCVFnXuO5E7hZktWY2qPtUbVNRrFjPMu9_PcrCuFZSBWhEfIcHmpS2GayFlvaZOf0Vp8FVpjQLc6EUmnttoFuUBo

As a creator, you are responsible for ensuring your branded content is  
properly disclosed and follows our policies and all legal regulatory  
requirements. We're here to equip you with the right features to maintain  
viewer trust and keep growing. Thanks for creating with us!

items.subject: [World Cube Association] Summary
items.summary: World Cube Association forum sent a weekly activity summary.
items.body:
A brief summary of [World Cube Association][1] since 2026-10-29 19:10:18 UTC

3 New Topics
2 Unread Notifications
93 New Users

  
  ### Popular Topics

    [Please don’t remove Clock][2]

      Removing Clock is out of this world unbelievable to me, why would they do that, FTO should replace FMC, NOT CLOCK, Clock is my favourite WCA event and removing it would ruin the community, firstly, it is so famous it surpasses Square-1 and Megaminx in popularity, secondly, FMC records don’t get broken as much as clock, the world record for FMC was set over 7 years ago but for Clock, it was broken just over a year ago, it is also 1 hour for each FMC attempt, that is 3 hours for the 3 attempts they give us, WCA competitions are meant to be about speed, FMC doesn’t do speed, you just need to find the shortest solution, don’t remove Clock, I am begging you

    
    [Potential unfair penalties in 4pad][3]

      I want to point out something I noticed while practicing at home that will likely make judging between a dnf and an ok solver harder on specific circunstances where there is no video footage. 
Because 4pad requires the small pads to be pressed to stop the timer, it is harder to false-stop (stop intencionally), which is good, but something that has happened to me a few times at home and I fear may happen in competitions, potencially resulting in extras or dnfs is me attempting to stop the timer, before touching the small pads realizing I have a +2, fix it and then properly stop the timer. I believe this will be hard to judge because the judge has reduced visibility of the small pads, I did press the big pads and everything happens in a very small time window. 
Although dnfs similar to this are possible in 2pad, it is much easier for the judge to determine if you actually stopped the timer in 2pad than in 4pad. 
I do not have a solution for this issue, and mainly just want to hear you al...

    
    [Should the scrambles included or showed with any competitor's ID?][4]

      Should the scrambles included or showed with any competitor’s best time or world record in his/her WCA ID? 
This be pretty helpful for community members and breakdown also and now navigating a scramble would also become easier. What are your all thoughts?

    

  

  ### Popular Posts

    Discgolfcubez - [WCA Asian Championship 2026 Cancellation][5]

    Maybe scroll up four posts and read for yourself :slightly_smiling_face:
    Clockisgood - [Changes to the WCA’s List of Official Events (June 2026)][6]

    While on the topic of the Clock poll, not sure if this has been raised before. 
The board had already voted and announced removal of Clock. 
Then decided to poll Delegates. Can everyone see the potential bias this creates. 
The people voting were elected by the Board and can be removed by the Board. When they are voting, don’t you think, that some who may be neutral, don’t really care or are slightly for Clock would have their vote influenced. 
‘The Board can see how I vote and they wanted to remove Clock. So I better vote to remove it, at least remove from major championships’. 
Imagine your bosses, teachers or parents, made a decision and then came and asked you about it. Would that not impact what you say. 
This is the main reason this decision stinks and needs to reversed. Put on hold, until a clear defined process is put in place.
    Clockisgood - [Changes to the WCA’s List of Official Events (June 2026)][7]

    Ok i concede that, but still the Board making their decision prior to the vote, will influence neutrals and those who do not care (dont compete in Clock or organise comps with it). 
Just remember, in the initial survey these same people voted against removing any event. 
This could be averted with a clear defined process, to avoid undue influence on voting members.
    Dovydas_Kirbutas - [The Removal of Clock Violates the WCA's Purpose and Values][8]
